questions.stem: The Nigerian Labour Law is a product of a multiplicity of sources broadly classified as legal and extra-legal sources. List and explain the sources of Labour Law in Nigeria. 17 marks.

All employees are workers, but not all workers are employees. There are therefore, two categories of workers in employment relationships. Explain these categories of workers, discussing the tests formulated by the courts in distinguishing them, and the necessity for the distinction. Support your answers with case law. 18 marks.

A contract of employment creates rights and obligations for parties therein. With the aid of case law and statutory provisions, explain the duties of the parties to a contract of employment. 18 Marks.
Discuss the concept of vicarious liability and explain circumstances that will make the employer liable for the acts of his employee. 17 Marks.

a) Mrs. Andrew, a civil servant, submitted her resignation letter. Two days later, her ministry terminated her employment for alleged misconduct discovered earlier. As a student versed in labour law, advise her. 9 marks.

b) Mr. Ade works for TechFirm Ltd. He was accused of leaking sensitive customer data. Without issuing a query, inviting him to respond or holding any hearing, the company wrote to him stating “You are dismissed with immediate effect for breach of trust”. Ade was never shown evidence. Critically analyze the lawfulness of this dismissal. 8 marks.

Mr. Okokon, a driver with the University of Calabar, took the Director of Works to Ikom and was directed to return to Calabar the same day. On his way back, Okokon branched at Odukpani to see his girlfriend and have a drink. While at Odukpani, his vehicle was involved in an accident. Mr. Essien who works in Unical, closed from work and went to visit Mr. Etim who resides at the Staff Quarters, to fix his broken air-conditioner. While carrying out the work, his spanner fell on Nsikak’s head and injured him. In the course of buying fuel at a filling station, Mr. Kenneth who drove an official car, lit a cigarette and this caused a fire outbreak that destroyed two cars.

With your knowledge of labour law, discuss the legal implications of the above scenarios. 18 Marks.
